h: Swallows climbing and the best of Swale
p: A session on the walls is quick and intense, which makes it perfect for slotting into a busy weekend. Allow a couple of hours for the whole visit, including check-in, harness fitting and the safety briefing, and arrive with a few minutes to spare so nobody feels rushed.

Each climber needs a participation form, with a parent or guardian signing for under-18s. Fill it in online before you leave home and you'll get through the desk faster. Check the age guidance when you book, too, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for younger children.

Top climbing tips? Use your legs, not your arms. Look up for the next hold. And when your nerve's tested at the top of a jump, just breathe, focus on the target and trust the line. Eat light beforehand and bring a water bottle.

Once you're done, there's more around Sittingbourne than people expect. Milton Creek Country Park, on land reclaimed beside the creek, has easy paths, a play area and plenty of space to explore. The Sittingbourne and Kemsley Light Railway is a heritage narrow-gauge line that runs on selected days, a lovely treat for little train fans, so check its timetable before you go. Faversham is close by for a historic town centre and market, and Leysdown on the Isle of Sheppey has the classic seaside feel if you fancy a run out to the coast.
